points.description: States that in a doubly-linked list insertion and deletion operations can be performed in constant time, O(1).
points.partial_credit: Half (1 mark) if says insertion/deletion is efficient or fast but does not state constant time/O(1), or gives constant time for only one of insertion or deletion.

points.description: States that this constant time holds for operations before a given location (at the node preceding a given position), because each node has a pointer to its previous node so no traversal from the head is needed.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.75) if mentions previous pointers/backward traversal but does not link it to constant-time operations before a given location.

points.description: States that constant-time operations also hold at the end of the list (e.g., deleting/inserting at the tail), whereas in a basic singly-linked list these require traversal (linear time) to find the preceding node.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.75) if mentions the end of the list but does not contrast with singly-linked list needing linear traversal, or vice versa.

rubric.notes: Full marks need constant time (O(1)) for insertion and deletion stated explicitly, including before a given location and at the end of the list, with the contrast to a basic list needing traversal. Vague answers such as "can move both directions" or "more flexible" earn nothing unless tied to constant-time operations. A wrong claim (e.g., faster search or less memory) loses the point it affects.
